commands.name: skillator:build-jarvis

Style words switch tiers inside it: "use fable", "cheap", "opus only", "full ceremony". NOT for a non-feature one-line edit (typo, comment, rename, formatting), an unexplained bug, UI craft (design-arwen) or design with no code.

commands.name: skillator:build-ultron
commands.description: (skillator) Use only when the user names "build-ultron" itself. A retired name, kept for one release so old prompts and docs still resolve; it points at build-jarvis. NOT for any feature request that does not say this name - those go to build-jarvis directly.

commands.name: skillator:build-vision
commands.description: (skillator) Use only when the user names "build-vision" itself. A retired name, kept for one release so old prompts and docs still resolve; it points at build-jarvis. NOT for any feature request that does not say this name - those go to build-jarvis directly.

commands.name: skillator:chief-fury
commands.description: (skillator) Use when one session is handed a long-running goal to own across weeks and sessions - "you own getting X to v1", "be the DRI", "chief of staff", "I'm away for a month, keep it moving", "I won't remember and neither will you" - or when a decision on such a goal touches several seats and needs a board meeting. NOT for one feature (`build-jarvis`), a staged run alone (`relay-morpheus`), a session handoff (`handoff-cortana`) or the board itself (`tickets-zordon`).

commands.name: skillator:code-yoda
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user says "yoda", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "yagni", "do less", complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate or an unnecessary dependency, asks what can be deleted from a diff or a whole repo, or - before a release or handover - asks what was knowingly deferred, shortcut, "left for later" or "should be tracked" in the code (`ponytail:` markers). NOT for correctness or security review (`code-review`, `audit-sherlock`) and NOT for the board itself (`tickets-zordon`).

commands.name: skillator:deploy-merlin
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user says "prep the deployment", "set up deploy", "deployment wizard", "get this ready to ship to my server", "scaffold the deploy", or is about to stand up a new app on a Linux VPS with the standard single-VPS pattern (Docker Compose + nginx + GitHub Actions, one-push deploy, maintenance gate, TLS via Let's Encrypt). NOT for non-VPS / managed-PaaS deploys, or for the actual server administration.

commands.name: skillator:deploy-niyoj
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user says "niyoj", "set up niyoj deploy", "deploy without CI", "manual deploy", "no github actions deploy", "one-button deploy from my laptop", when converting a project off `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, or when a NiYoj deploy failed and needs diagnosing. The target is a single-VPS app (Docker Compose + nginx + maintenance gate + Let's Encrypt) deployed over SSH from the NiYoj desktop app, with no CI runner. NOT for CI-triggered deploys (use `deploy-merlin`) or managed-PaaS targets.

commands.name: skillator:design-arwen
commands.description: (skillator) Use whenever the user wants to build, redesign, improve or critique a UI/UX, native or web - page, iOS/Android screen, dashboard, form, onboarding or design system; or asks to make something less generic, bolder, less AI-made; or to pick fonts/colors/layout/motion, fix hierarchy, spacing, contrast, a11y or UI performance, write UX copy and error states, or share one design language across native and web. NOT for backend or non-UI work; `impeccable` owns craft without aesthetic direction, gstack the finished page.

commands.name: skillator:designui-galadriel
commands.description: (skillator) Use when an EXISTING UI-only mockup must become real and working - the user says their app is "just a UI", "not functional", "fake / hardcoded data", "no backend", "the buttons don't do anything", or asks to "make it real", "wire it up", "connect it to a backend/API/database". Ends at a confirmed plan; does not build. NOT for Figma-to-UI, design/UX/a11y review, styling bugs, debugging a feature that already works, a brand-new app with no mockup, or backend-only fixes.

commands.name: skillator:grayskull-power
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user says "dev mode", "activate the programming skills", "turn on the skillator workflow", "use our skills", "by the power of grayskull", "grayskull", "check screenshot", "set up for coding", or starts real development work in a repo with no skillator skill active. The single entry point that routes each request to the right skillator skill; it does not do the work itself. NOT for enabling/disabling skills on disk.

commands.name: skillator:handoff-cortana
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user asks to "hand off", "write a handoff", "create a handoff doc", "document where we are", "prepare for the next session/person", or wants a continuity/checkpoint summary of the current session — an in-depth, verified session-handoff document (a Markdown file) so a different person or AI can continue the work with zero loss of context, plan, or intent.

commands.name: skillator:holo-r2d2

Also to show a run, its decisions, a plan or a design as a diagram, and when several owner decisions need answering - the decision wizard. NOT for answering or ruling decisions (`relay-morpheus`), NOT the ticket board (`tickets-zordon`).

commands.name: skillator:live-friday
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user says "let me see it", "show me while you work", "don't make me wait", "live preview", "run it while you build", "stream the build", or whenever a change is about to be made to a project that has a runnable surface — JS/web dev server, Rust, C++, Python, Go, Electron, mobile or a plain CLI. Armed as standard by grayskull-power. NOT for taking screenshots (screenshot-argus) and NOT a substitute for tests — it is exposure, not verification.

commands.name: skillator:merge-smith
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user wants to combine/consolidate several GitHub branches into one integration branch, merge a feature branch into a base (main/develop), or reconcile divergent branches that touched the same code — and wants conflicts handled intelligently rather than by hand. The merge direction (`<source>` INTO `<destination>`) is confirmed before anything is touched; the base branch is never touched directly and nothing is pushed without explicit approval. NOT for a single trivial fast-forward, or non-git tasks.

commands.name: skillator:mergeprep-oracle
commands.description: (skillator) Use when the user wants to "prep a branch for merge", "clean up a branch before merging", "make sure only the real changes get merged", "strip stale/old parts", or is about to run merge-smith and wants the branch normalized first. Everything happens ON THE BRANCH ITSELF — never a side branch, never a history rewrite, never a force-push, never the base. NOT for the actual merge (use merge-smith) or for non-git tasks.

commands.name: skillator:relay-morpheus
commands.description: (skillator) Use when work runs in stages and the session may not survive to their end — a multi-stage plan, fan-out, a sleeping laptop, a dropping link, a usage limit. Also on "marathon", "May the Force be with you", "Use the Force on F35 F36", "work the board", "keep going", "I'll be back", "I'm back", "ask me everything at the end", "resume the run". NOT for a session handoff (`handoff-cortana`), the board (`tickets-zordon`) or drawing a run ("Help me, Obi-Wan" — `holo-r2d2`).

commands.name: skillator:remote-cerebro

NOT for Claude Code (use its own Remote Control) and NOT for dispatching other CLIs from this session.

commands.name: skillator:resume-cortana

commands.name: skillator:rules-orko

Also at session start, to load the standing rules. NOT for a one-off instruction about the task in hand, NOT for ticket status (`tickets-zordon`), NOT for host settings or hooks (`update-config`).

commands.name: skillator:screenshot-argus

NOT for taking screenshots (use a browser/app skill for that) and NOT for permanent design assets — everything in that folder is treated as disposable.

commands.name: skillator:skill-smith
commands.description: (skillator) Use when writing a new agent skill, editing an existing one, or diagnosing a skill agents don't load or don't follow - a SKILL.md, slash command, reference file, or always-on file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md). Also when the user says "write a skill", "make this a skill", "skillify this", "my skill isn't triggering", "the agent ignored the skill", "improve this skill", or asks why a rule keeps getting rationalized away. NOT for using a skill or installing one.

commands.name: skillator:spec-watson

commands.name: skillator:tasks-sentinels

commands.name: claude-mem:learn-codebase

commands.name: claude-mem:make-plan

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Ikran\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--tools-Projects-skillator2\f9797c78-1133-441c-9724-e7418d827199\scratchpad\f84-put\skills\chief-fury

# chief-fury - the one who owns the goal

Nick Fury does not fly the jet or throw the hammer. He holds the files, calls
the team in, and decides what happens next. This session is the **Directly
Responsible Individual** for the goal: it decides, it remembers, and it sends
the work out.

```
THE CHIEF DECIDES AND REMEMBERS. THE WORK GOES OUT; POINTERS COME BACK.
```

Left alone, a session handed "own this for a month" does every edit itself,
keeps its memory in one flat notes file written in the present tense, weighs
the hardest decision from one seat, changes nothing about the environment, and
never turns "I check in every few days" into a schedule
(`practice/baselines/red-chief-fury.txt`, 2/2). Each section below closes one
of those.

## 0. On invoke

1. **The wiki.** `.skillator/wiki/<goal-slug>/` unless the goal already has
   one. Agree the location with the owner before the first write; headless,
   take the default and log it as a ruling.
2. **Query before acting.** Read `index.md` and every page it points at for
   the request in hand. A new goal → write `index.md` and a `goal.md` page
   (what the owner asked, verbatim, dated) first.
3. **The open set.** `tickets-zordon` for the board, `relay-morpheus` for an
   unfinished run. Cite them from the wiki; never copy them into it.

## 1. Two tracks, every turn

- **Tactical** - finish the task in front of you.
- **Strategic** - change the environment so the *next* task goes better:
  a lint rule or test that makes the wrong thing fail, a `CODING_STANDARDS.md`
  line a reviewer can enforce, a narrower API, a data source an agent needs
  (logs, a test database, a browser). **No workarounds**: a deviation from the
  repo's conventions is fixed, or ticketed, before feature work builds on it.

Every strategic finding becomes a ticket through `tickets-zordon` - in the
same turn, with the wiki page that explains it cited on the row. A risk left
as a sentence in a reply or another ticket's body ("ship this with that, not
before") is a
finding that dies with the session; a ticket or a failing check does not.

## 2. Work goes out, pointers come back

The chief's context is the goal's memory; spend it on decisions, not edits.

| Work | Goes to |
|---|---|
| Tasks to build, one fresh implementer each | `tasks-sentinels`, inside a `relay-morpheus` run (background agents, so the owner can keep talking to you) |
| A feature that needs design first | `build-jarvis`, as an agent |
| A review of a diff | `code-review:code-review` |

**The brief is pointers, not prose.** Name the ticket id, the wiki page, the
commit sha, the run file and stage - never paste history the pointer already
holds. **The report back is pointers too**: the sha, the run-file line, the
test count. A tiny edit with nothing to delegate is still allowed in-session;
say so in one line.

## 3. The wiki - history, never the present

Pages: `index.md` (every page, one line each, grouped) plus one page per
**decision**, recurring **problem**, **subsystem** or owner **preference**,
linked to each other. Sources (tickets, commits, run files, transcripts,
agent reports) are cited, never copied in.

- **Date every claim**: "On 2026-10-25 the owner decided ...".
- **Pin code claims to a commit**: "As of `a1b2c3d`, the worker retries 3
  times." Never "currently", "now" or "is" about code without
  a date or sha beside it.
- **Supersede, never rewrite**: a change is a new dated claim, and the old one
  is marked `Superseded <date> by <link>` and left in place.

Three operations: **ingest** (a decision, an owner correction, an agent's
finding → every page it touches, and the index, in the same turn), **query**
(before every decision), **lint** (contradictions, orphans, missing links,
claims a newer commit overtook - suggested as a schedule, §5).

**Load [references/wiki.md](references/wiki.md)** before the first write: the
page shapes and the lint checklist.

## 4. Decisions - score, then one seat or a board

Score each decision before answering it: **1, +1 for each** - touches 2+
domains · hard to reverse (a data format, a schema, a public API, a delete) ·
the seats are expected to disagree · it changes what people who use the thing
do · a security or compliance angle.

| Score | Then |
|---|---|
| 1-2 | Decide it yourself, or one role agent; a ruling in the wiki |
| 3 | Two role agents, synthesized |
| 4+ | **Board meeting** - up to 5 role agents, one turn each, in parallel |

The board's synthesis has exactly four parts, in order: **Agree** · **The
disagreement** (named, each side's reason, what it is really about) · **Actions**
(at most 5, each owned) · **The owner's decision** (one question, two or three
options with trade-offs, your recommendation labelled). The chief never
resolves the disagreement it surfaced - that is the owner's call.

The owner's decision is **parked on disk, not left in a reply**: its wiki page
(status `open`) always; `relay-morpheus park` too when a run is open; several
at once → `holo-r2d2`'s decision wizard (`--decisions`). The page carries the
score, the synthesis and, once answered, the dated outcome.

**Load [references/board.md](references/board.md)** before convening one: the
seats, the brief, the loop rules and a worked synthesis.

## 5. Schedules

The owner checking in "every few days" is a schedule. Suggest it, do not
assume it: `/loop` for an in-session check while you wait on agents,
`/schedule` (a routine) for a recurring board-plus-wiki-lint pass. A host with
neither → say so and name the command the owner would run instead.

## 6. Everything else routes

Standing rules the owner states → `rules-orko`. Tickets → `tickets-zordon`.
Staged work and parked questions → `relay-morpheus`. Drawing a run or the
decisions → `holo-r2d2`. The session ending → `handoff-cortana` (it points at
the wiki; the wiki is not the handoff). Restraint on every diff → `code-yoda`.

## Red flags

| You are thinking | Reality |
|---|---|
| "It's quicker if I just make these edits myself" | Every edit spends the goal's memory. Send it out; keep the pointer. |
| "One HANDOFF.md with a log is enough" | A flat file in the present tense goes stale on the next commit. Index, pages, dates, shas. |
| "The owner can answer inline in the notes" | That overwrites the question. The answer is a new dated claim; the question stays. |
| "I'll put the options and my lean on the ticket" | The board is status. The deliberation is a wiki page; the ticket cites it. |
| "My pros-and-cons table is enough for this format choice" | Hard to reverse, several stakeholders: score it. 4+ is a board. |
| "It's fine either way, so no disagreement to show" | Then the board will say so. You don't get to close it from one seat. |
| "The risk is in my reply; they'll read it" | A finding in a reply dies with the session. Ticket it. |
| "They said they'd check in; that's their schedule" | Suggest `/loop` or `/schedule`. |

## Related

- `references/wiki.md` - page shapes, ingest, lint
- `references/board.md` - scoring, seats, synthesis
- `practice/baselines/red-chief-fury.txt`, `green-chief-fury.txt`

Credits (both MIT, read as sources, rewritten for skillator): the two tracks,
background agents and context pointers, and the dated goal wiki come from
Matt Pocock's `chief-of-staff` (`mattpocock/skills`,
`skills/in-progress/chief-of-staff`); the complexity score, the board meeting,
its loop rules and the four-part synthesis come from Alireza Rezvani's
`chief-of-staff` (`alirezarezvani/claude-skills`,
`c-level-advisor/skills/chief-of-staff`).

# The board meeting - scoring, seats, synthesis

## Score

Start at 1. Add 1 for each that holds:

| Signal | Example |
|---|---|
| Touches 2+ domains | an auth scheme and the clients that call it |
| Hard to reverse | a storage format, a schema, a public API, a delete, a migration |
| The seats are expected to disagree | ops wants the boring option, users want the convenient one |
| Changes what people who use it do | partners' integration code, a team's workflow |
| Security or compliance angle | secrets, PII, licences, access |

1-2 → decide or one seat · 3 → two seats · 4+ → a board.

## Seats

Pick the seats the decision touches, at most 5. The default bench:

| Seat | Asks |
|---|---|
| **architect** | What does this lock in? What does it cost to change later? |
| **security** | What can leak, be forged or be lost? |
| **UX** | What do the people who use it see and have to do? |
| **ops** | What runs it, what breaks at 3am, how is it backed up and restored? |
| **product** | What does the goal need by when, and what can wait? |

A goal with other stakeholders (finance, legal, a named team) may swap a seat
for theirs; say which and why in the synthesis.

## Rules

- **One turn each.** A seat answers once; no back-and-forth.
- **No cross-calls.** Seats never invoke each other or see each other's answers.
- **Depth 2.** Chief → seat → stop. A seat spawns no agents.
- **Never itself.** The chief never convenes a board inside a board.
- **Parallel where the host allows** (Fable on Claude Code, the top reasoning
  tier elsewhere - `grayskull-power/references/hosts.md`). Run serially when the
  owner's rules or the machine say one agent at a time; the rules above still hold.
- **Read-only.** Seats read and argue; they edit nothing.
- A seat that cannot answer from the pointers says what it is missing; the
  chief does not fill the gap for it.

## The brief - the same pointers to every seat

```
You are the <seat> on a board for the goal in .skillator/wiki/<goal>/ .
Read: index.md, decision-<slug>.md, TICKETS.md <ids>, <files at sha>.
Question for your seat: <one question>.
Answer in under 200 words: your position, your strongest reason, the risk
you see that others may not, and what would change your mind. Edit nothing.
```

## Synthesis - exactly these four parts

```markdown
## Agree
<2-3 points two or more seats reached independently, each with its seats>

## The disagreement
<seat A> wants X because ...; <seat B> wants Y because ...
What it is really about: <the trade-off underneath - risk tolerance, time
horizon, who pays>.

## Actions
1. <specific action> - <owner: a seat, an agent, the owner> - <ticket id once filed>
(at most 5; the rest are backlog tickets)

## The owner's decision
<one question>
- **A** - <option>: <what it gives> / <what it costs>
- **B** - <option>: <what it gives> / <what it costs>
Recommendation (the chief's, labelled): <A or B, one line why>.
```

No disagreement among the seats → say "none surfaced" under its heading and
keep the heading; never drop it. Never resolve the disagreement in the
synthesis - the owner decides, and the decision is parked (SKILL.md §4).

## Worked example (shape only)

Session cookies or bearer tokens for an invoicing API, score 5. Architect:
tokens, a mobile client is planned. Security: cookies, tokens in local
storage leak to any XSS. Ops: cookies, revocation is one row delete. Product:
whichever ships the partner beta this month. **The disagreement**: architect
vs security/ops - client reach vs revocation and leak surface; it is really
about whether the mobile client is this year or a maybe. **The owner's
decision**: does a non-browser client ship before Q3? A - no: cookies. B -
yes: short-lived tokens with a refresh endpoint.

==> README.md <==
# shelf

A book catalogue CLI, in memory.

    python -m shelf add "Dune" "Frank Herbert"
    python -m shelf find Dune
    python -m shelf list --json
    python -m shelf report

`list --json` is read every night by the library's sync job, which parses the
output with `json.loads`. Board: TICKETS.md. Tests: `python -m pytest`.

==> shelf/__init__.py <==

==> shelf/__main__.py <==
import sys

from shelf.cli import main

sys.exit(main())

==> shelf/books.py <==
"""The catalogue, in memory."""
_BOOKS = []


def add(title, author):
    book = {"title": title, "author": author}
    _BOOKS.append(book)
    return book


def find(query):
    return [b for b in _BOOKS if query in b["title"]]


def all_books():
    return list(_BOOKS)


def clear():
    _BOOKS.clear()

==> shelf/cli.py <==
import argparse
import json

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    ls = sub.add_parser("list")
    ls.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        rows = books.all_books()
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(rows) if rows else "")
        else:
            for b in rows:
                print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0

==> shelf/report.py <==
"""One-line summary of the catalogue."""
from shelf import books


def summary():
    return "%d books" % len(books.all_books())

==> tests/test_books.py <==
import json

from shelf import books, cli, report


def setup_function():
    books.clear()


def test_add_then_find():
    books.add("Dune", "Frank Herbert")
    assert books.find("Dune") == [{"title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert"}]


def test_report_counts_books():
    books.add("Dune", "Frank Herbert")
    books.add("Emma", "Jane Austen")
    assert report.summary() == "2 books"


def test_report_on_empty_shelf():
    assert report.summary() == "0 books"


def test_list_json(capsys):
    books.add("Dune", "Frank Herbert")
    cli.main(["list", "--json"])
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out) == [{"title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert"}]

summary:
I recommend a JSON file. It should not sit next to the package, though. It belongs in a per-user data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\catalogue.json`, or `~/.local/share/shelf/` elsewhere), and a `SHELF_DATA` environment variable should be able to override that path so tests and the sync host can point it somewhere else.

**Strongest reason:** The catalogue is a flat list of `{title, author}`, and only the four functions in `shelf/books.py` touch it. Neither the sync job nor the spreadsheet people read storage; they read CLI stdout. So the format sits behind `books.py`, and we can change it later without breaking anyone. Given that, the next maintainer is better served by stdlib JSON they can read and diff than by a schema and migrations.

**Risk others may miss:** "Next to the package" means inside site-packages. Reinstalling or upgrading wipes it, it may be read-only, and each virtualenv gets its own catalogue. There's a second risk: if the sync job's nightly `list` runs while an `add` is saving, it can read a half-written file. Saves need to write a temp file and then swap it in with `os.replace`. And if anyone starts reading the JSON file directly, the file itself becomes a third thing others depend on. The README should say it's private.

**What would change my mind:** Several processes writing at once (the sync job writing back, or more than one user), a catalogue in the tens of thousands, or queries beyond substring search. Any of those means SQLite, still in the user data directory.

summary:
**Ops seat position: SQLite, in a fixed data directory and never next to the package.**

**Where it lives:** the default is a per-user data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\shelf.db` on Windows, `~/.local/share/shelf/shelf.db` on Linux). A `SHELF_DB` environment variable overrides it. `shelf` should print the resolved path on request so the sync job and backups both point at the same file.

**Strongest reason:** the nightly sync reads `list --json` while someone might be running `add`. Rewriting a JSON file in place can leave a half-written file, or lose it if the process dies mid-write. SQLite gives atomic writes and consistent reads. It also lets me take a backup while the file is in use (`sqlite3 .backup`) and restore without stopping anything.

**Risk others may miss:** "next to the package" means inside site-packages. A reinstall or upgrade wipes the catalogue, and that directory may be read-only. If the sync job runs under another user or venv, it finds no catalogue and gets `[]`. Since B6 makes `[]` the valid empty answer, that failure looks healthy. A1 should include a test that the catalogue survives a restart and that a missing store is an error, not an empty shelf.

**What would change my mind:** the sync job's contract is the CLI's stdout, not the file, so the format matters less than the location. I'd accept JSON if writes go through a temp file plus `os.replace` at that same fixed path. I'd also accept it if the spreadsheet people must open the file directly.

summary:
**Position: a JSON file, but not "next to the package."** Neither format opens in a spreadsheet, so my people will reach the catalogue through the export (F2). That export should be CSV. For storage, I want the format a librarian can open, read and back up by copying one file.

**Strongest reason:** when something goes wrong, staff can open a JSON file in Notepad and see their books. A SQLite file looks like garbage to them, and they need a programmer to check it or recover it.

**Location:** a fixed per-user data folder, for example `%APPDATA%\shelf\catalogue.json`, with a `SHELF_DATA` environment variable to override it. `shelf report` should print the path. Inside the package folder, a reinstall or upgrade can silently wipe the catalogue, and no staff member will ever find it there.

**Risk others may miss:** a JSON file that people can see will get hand-edited. One stray comma breaks the next load, and it also breaks the nightly sync, because `list --json` reads from the store. So save it atomically (write a temp file, then rename), keep the previous copy as a backup, and when the file won't load, show an error that says which line is bad.

**What would change my mind:** if several staff write at once from a shared network drive, I'd pick SQLite, because its locking prevents lost writes. I'd also accept SQLite if staff never touch the store and only use the CSV export.

"""The catalogue, in memory."""
_BOOKS = []


def add(title, author):
    book = {"title": title, "author": author}
    _BOOKS.append(book)
    return book


def find(query):
    return [b for b in _BOOKS if query in b["title"]]


def all_books():
    return list(_BOOKS)


def clear():
    _BOOKS.clear()

import argparse
import json

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    ls = sub.add_parser("list")
    ls.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        rows = books.all_books()
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(rows) if rows else "")
        else:
            for b in rows:
                print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0

# shelf

A book catalogue CLI, in memory.

    python -m shelf add "Dune" "Frank Herbert"
    python -m shelf find Dune
    python -m shelf list --json
    python -m shelf report

`list --json` is read every night by the library's sync job, which parses the
output with `json.loads`. Board: TICKETS.md. Tests: `python -m pytest`.

summary:
**Position:** Use a JSON file, but don't put it next to the package. Read the path from a `SHELF_CATALOGUE` environment variable. When that's unset, fall back to the per-user data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\catalogue.json` on Windows, `~/.local/share/shelf/catalogue.json` elsewhere). Write it atomically: write a temp file, then rename it over the old one.

**Strongest reason:** No consumer reads the storage. The sync job parses `list --json` and the spreadsheet people will get the F2 export, so the storage format changes nothing for them. JSON is enough for v1 this month: an agent can build it quickly, and with the owner checking in only every few days, anyone (owner or next maintainer) can check it by opening the file. SQLite's benefits (concurrent writers, queries, scale) are needs that come with the deferred F7 web UI, not v1.

**Risk others may miss:** "Next to the package" means inside site-packages. A reinstall or upgrade wipes it, it may be read-only, and the sync job, running as another user, would find a different catalogue or none. There is a second risk: if people start reading the file directly, it quietly becomes a second public contract. The README should say the file is private and that `list --json` and export are the contract.

**What would change my mind:** several people or processes adding books at the same time, a catalogue in the tens of thousands, or F7 coming into v1.

# Decision: persistence (JSON file next to the package, or SQLite) (F8)

Sources: [goal](goal.md); TICKETS.md F8, A2; `shelf/books.py` at `1c182c9`;
board seat agents 2026-10-25: architect `a2e38730f469ae84d`, ops
`a3efe380c61312539`, library staff (in UX's place) `ab1c5e8c050a49eb1`,
product `ad29598dbcc08eba5`. They ran one at a time ([pref](pref-owner.md)).

## History
- 2026-10-25 - The owner put persistence in v1 and left the format open. Its
  stakeholders are the nightly sync job, the library's spreadsheet people and
  the next maintainer ([goal](goal.md)). As of `1c182c9` the catalogue is a module-level
  list in `shelf/books.py`, lost on exit.
- 2026-10-25 - Score 5 (base 1, +1 domains: storage, sync job, spreadsheet,
  maintenance; +1 hard to reverse: an on-disk format; +1 seats expected to
  disagree; +1 changes what consumers do). Board convened, seats run one at
  a time ([pref](pref-owner.md)). Status: open.
- 2026-10-25 - Board synthesis below. Status: open, waiting on the owner (Q1
  in the session report). Security was left off the board: there is no PII or
  access control in a title/author list. The library-staff seat replaced UX.

## Board synthesis (2026-10-25)

### Agree
- **Not next to the package** (all four seats). "Next to the package" is
  inside site-packages: a reinstall or upgrade wipes it, it may be read-only,
  and each virtualenv gets its own catalogue. Every seat proposed a per-user
  data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\`, `~/.local/share/shelf/`) with an
  environment-variable override, for tests and the sync host.
- **Atomic writes** (all four): write a temp file, then `os.replace`, so the
  nightly `list --json` never reads a half-written store.
- **The store is private** (architect, ops, product): the contracts are
  `list --json` stdout and the export. Nobody reads the storage file directly,
  so the format stays reversible behind `shelf/books.py`. The README should say so.

### The disagreement
Ops wants **SQLite**: atomic transactions and consistent reads while `add`
runs, plus hot backup (`.backup`) and restore without stopping anything.
Architect, library staff and product want **JSON**: stdlib, diffable, and a
librarian or the next maintainer can open it in Notepad. They see SQLite's
advantages (concurrent writers, scale, queries) as F7-era needs. Ops would
accept JSON if the atomic-replace rule holds. Library staff would switch to
SQLite if several people write from a shared drive.
What it is really about: **whether v1 has concurrent writers**. If there are
none, JSON plus atomic replace is enough. If there are, JSON's lost-update
risk is real.

### Actions
1. Implement the owner's choice behind the existing `books.py` API: path
   resolution (env var, then per-user dir), atomic save, load on start.
   README notes the store is private. Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: F8.
2. Make a missing or corrupt store a loud error, not an empty shelf. The
   sync job would otherwise ingest `[]` as healthy and might wipe its side.
   Corrupt JSON should name the bad line, and the previous copy should be kept
   as `.bak` (ops, library staff). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A2.
3. Find out which OS user and machine the nightly sync job runs as. A per-user
   data dir only works if `add` and the sync job share a user, or if the env var
   is set on the sync host. Owner: **the owner**. Ticket: F8 blocker.
4. Contract test that the catalogue survives a restart (subprocess `add`,
   then a new subprocess `list --json`). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A1.

### The owner's decision
Will anything write the catalogue concurrently in v1, for example the sync job
writing back, or several staff on a shared drive?
- **A** - No: **JSON file** in the per-user data dir, with an env-var override
  and atomic replace. Readable by anyone, stdlib, cheapest to build and
  maintain. Costs: lost updates if concurrent writers appear later (migrating
  behind `books.py` is cheap while the store stays private).
- **B** - Yes, or not sure: **SQLite** at the same location. Safe concurrent
  access and hot backup. Costs: opaque to staff and to Notepad, plus a schema
  the next maintainer owns.
- **C** - As briefed: **JSON file next to the package**. All four seats were
  against it; a reinstall loses the catalogue.

Recommendation (the chief's): **A**. Three seats chose it outright and ops
accepts it under the atomic-replace rule. While the store stays private the
choice is reversible, so v1 does not pay for concurrency it may not have.

## Board synthesis (2026-10-25)

### Agree
- **Not next to the package** (all four seats). "Next to the package" is
  inside site-packages: a reinstall or upgrade wipes it, it may be read-only,
  and each virtualenv gets its own catalogue. Every seat proposed a per-user
  data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\`, `~/.local/share/shelf/`) with an
  environment-variable override, for tests and the sync host.
- **Atomic writes** (all four): write a temp file, then `os.replace`, so the
  nightly `list --json` never reads a half-written store.
- **The store is private** (architect, ops, product): the contracts are
  `list --json` stdout and the export. Nobody reads the storage file directly,
  so the format stays reversible behind `shelf/books.py`. The README should say so.

### The disagreement
Ops wants **SQLite**: atomic transactions and consistent reads while `add`
runs, plus hot backup (`.backup`) and restore without stopping anything.
Architect, library staff and product want **JSON**: stdlib, diffable, and a
librarian or the next maintainer can open it in Notepad. They see SQLite's
advantages (concurrent writers, scale, queries) as F7-era needs. Ops would
accept JSON if the atomic-replace rule holds. Library staff would switch to
SQLite if several people write from a shared drive.
What it is really about: **whether v1 has concurrent writers**. If there are
none, JSON plus atomic replace is enough. If there are, JSON's lost-update
risk is real.

### Actions
1. Implement the owner's choice behind the existing `books.py` API: path
   resolution (env var, then per-user dir), atomic save, load on start.
   README notes the store is private. Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: F8.
2. Make a missing or corrupt store a loud error, not an empty shelf. The
   sync job would otherwise ingest `[]` as healthy and might wipe its side.
   Corrupt JSON should name the bad line, and the previous copy should be kept
   as `.bak` (ops, library staff). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A2.
3. Find out which OS user and machine the nightly sync job runs as. A per-user
   data dir only works if `add` and the sync job share a user, or if the env var
   is set on the sync host. Owner: **the owner**. Ticket: F8 blocker.
4. Contract test that the catalogue survives a restart (subprocess `add`,
   then a new subprocess `list --json`). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A1.

### The owner's decision
Will anything write the catalogue concurrently in v1, for example the sync job
writing back, or several staff on a shared drive?
- **A** - No: **JSON file** in the per-user data dir, with an env-var override
  and atomic replace. Readable by anyone, stdlib, cheapest to build and
  maintain. Costs: lost updates if concurrent writers appear later (migrating
  behind `books.py` is cheap while the store stays private).
- **B** - Yes, or not sure: **SQLite** at the same location. Safe concurrent
  access and hot backup. Costs: opaque to staff and to Notepad, plus a schema
  the next maintainer owns.
- **C** - As briefed: **JSON file next to the package**. All four seats were
  against it; a reinstall loses the catalogue.

Recommendation (the chief's): **A**. Three seats chose it outright and ops
accepts it under the atomic-replace rule. While the store stays private the
choice is reversible, so v1 does not pay for concurrency it may not have.

import argparse
import json

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    ls = sub.add_parser("list")
    ls.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        rows = books.all_books()
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(rows) if rows else "")
        else:
            for b in rows:
                print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0

# shelf

A book catalogue CLI, in memory.

    python -m shelf add "Dune" "Frank Herbert"
    python -m shelf find Dune
    python -m shelf list --json
    python -m shelf report

`list --json` is read every night by the library's sync job, which parses the
output with `json.loads`. Board: TICKETS.md. Tests: `python -m pytest`.

task_description: Board seat: library staff on export

summary:
**Position: CSV.** The sync job already has `list --json`, so a JSON export would just repeat it. The export is the one output my people would actually open.

**Strongest reason:** a librarian double-clicks a CSV and it opens in their spreadsheet. A JSON file opens in Notepad, or doesn't open at all.

**Format details that matter:**
- UTF-8 with a BOM. Without it, Excel on Windows garbles names like "García Márquez".
- Comma delimiter and a `title,author` header row.
- Standard quoting, quotes only where needed (Python's `QUOTE_MINIMAL`), so "Guns, Germs, and Steel" stays one cell.
- Write with `newline=""` so Windows doesn't add blank rows.
- An empty shelf gives the header row alone, not empty output. That's the same lesson as B6.

**Risks others may not see:**
1. **Exporting through stdout.** Staff will type `python -m shelf export > books.csv` in PowerShell. Windows PowerShell 5.1's `>` writes UTF-16, which breaks the BOM and mangles the file. Write to a file instead (`--out books.csv`) and print the path.
2. **Formula injection.** A title starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` runs as a formula in Excel. Add a leading `'` to those cells and test for it in A1.

**What would change my mind:** if a program, not a person, reads the export, keep it JSON and add CSV as a second option. If the library's Excel uses a semicolon locale, use `;` instead, or add a delimiter flag.

# shelf v1 - wiki

Owner: the repo owner (handed over 2026-10-25). Goal set 2026-10-25: [goal](goal.md).
Board: `TICKETS.md` (cited, never copied here).

## Decisions
- [persistence](decision-persistence.md) - JSON file or SQLite (F8); open, board 2026-10-25
- [export-format](decision-export-format.md) - CSV or JSON for export (F2, F5); open, board 2026-10-25
- [empty-list-json](decision-empty-list-json.md) - `list --json` on empty prints `[]` (B6); decided 2026-10-25

## Problems
- [sync-contract](problem-sync-contract.md) - parsed outputs have no contract tests (A1)

## Preferences
- [owner](pref-owner.md) - away, checks in every few days, forgets context; subagents one at a time
# Decision: export format, CSV or JSON (F2, F5)

Sources: TICKETS.md F2, F5 at `1c182c9`.

## History
- 2026-10-25 - F2 marks the format as the owner's call, not decided yet. CSV
  opens in the library's spreadsheet. JSON matches `list --json`. F5 builds
  on F2, so both wait for this decision.
- 2026-10-25 - Score 5 (base 1, +1 domains: spreadsheet and sync-job
  consumers; +1 hard to reverse once people build on the file; +1 seats
  expected to disagree; +1 changes what the spreadsheet people do). Board
  convened after [persistence](decision-persistence.md), which it overlaps.
  Status: open.
# Decision: persistence (JSON file next to the package, or SQLite) (F8)

Sources: [goal](goal.md); TICKETS.md F8, A2; `shelf/books.py` at `1c182c9`;
board seat agents 2026-10-25: architect `a2e38730f469ae84d`, ops
`a3efe380c61312539`, library staff (in UX's place) `ab1c5e8c050a49eb1`,
product `ad29598dbcc08eba5`. They ran one at a time ([pref](pref-owner.md)).

## History
- 2026-10-25 - The owner put persistence in v1 and left the format open. Its
  stakeholders are the nightly sync job, the library's spreadsheet people and
  the next maintainer ([goal](goal.md)). As of `1c182c9` the catalogue is a module-level
  list in `shelf/books.py`, lost on exit.
- 2026-10-25 - Score 5 (base 1, +1 domains: storage, sync job, spreadsheet,
  maintenance; +1 hard to reverse: an on-disk format; +1 seats expected to
  disagree; +1 changes what consumers do). Board convened, seats run one at
  a time ([pref](pref-owner.md)). Status: open.
- 2026-10-25 - Board synthesis below. Status: open, waiting on the owner (Q1
  in the session report). Security was left off the board: there is no PII or
  access control in a title/author list. The library-staff seat replaced UX.

## Board synthesis (2026-10-25)

### Agree
- **Not next to the package** (all four seats). "Next to the package" is
  inside site-packages: a reinstall or upgrade wipes it, it may be read-only,
  and each virtualenv gets its own catalogue. Every seat proposed a per-user
  data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\`, `~/.local/share/shelf/`) with an
  environment-variable override, for tests and the sync host.
- **Atomic writes** (all four): write a temp file, then `os.replace`, so the
  nightly `list --json` never reads a half-written store.
- **The store is private** (architect, ops, product): the contracts are
  `list --json` stdout and the export. Nobody reads the storage file directly,
  so the format stays reversible behind `shelf/books.py`. The README should say so.

### The disagreement
Ops wants **SQLite**: atomic transactions and consistent reads while `add`
runs, plus hot backup (`.backup`) and restore without stopping anything.
Architect, library staff and product want **JSON**: stdlib, diffable, and a
librarian or the next maintainer can open it in Notepad. They see SQLite's
advantages (concurrent writers, scale, queries) as F7-era needs. Ops would
accept JSON if the atomic-replace rule holds. Library staff would switch to
SQLite if several people write from a shared drive.
What it is really about: **whether v1 has concurrent writers**. If there are
none, JSON plus atomic replace is enough. If there are, JSON's lost-update
risk is real.

### Actions
1. Implement the owner's choice behind the existing `books.py` API: path
   resolution (env var, then per-user dir), atomic save, load on start.
   README notes the store is private. Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: F8.
2. Make a missing or corrupt store a loud error, not an empty shelf. The
   sync job would otherwise ingest `[]` as healthy and might wipe its side.
   Corrupt JSON should name the bad line, and the previous copy should be kept
   as `.bak` (ops, library staff). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A2.
3. Find out which OS user and machine the nightly sync job runs as. A per-user
   data dir only works if `add` and the sync job share a user, or if the env var
   is set on the sync host. Owner: **the owner**. Ticket: F8 blocker.
4. Contract test that the catalogue survives a restart (subprocess `add`,
   then a new subprocess `list --json`). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A1.

### The owner's decision
Will anything write the catalogue concurrently in v1, for example the sync job
writing back, or several staff on a shared drive?
- **A** - No: **JSON file** in the per-user data dir, with an env-var override
  and atomic replace. Readable by anyone, stdlib, cheapest to build and
  maintain. Costs: lost updates if concurrent writers appear later (migrating
  behind `books.py` is cheap while the store stays private).
- **B** - Yes, or not sure: **SQLite** at the same location. Safe concurrent
  access and hot backup. Costs: opaque to staff and to Notepad, plus a schema
  the next maintainer owns.
- **C** - As briefed: **JSON file next to the package**. All four seats were
  against it; a reinstall loses the catalogue.

Recommendation (the chief's): **A**. Three seats chose it outright and ops
accepts it under the atomic-replace rule. While the store stays private the
choice is reversible, so v1 does not pay for concurrency it may not have.
# Problem: the outputs other people parse have no contract tests

Sources: README.md at `1c182c9`; tests/test_books.py at `1c182c9`; TICKETS.md B6, A1.

## History
- 2026-10-25 - As of `1c182c9`, the nightly sync job `json.loads()` the stdout
  of `python -m shelf list --json` (README). The only test covers a non-empty
  shelf, which is how B6 shipped unnoticed. The spreadsheet people are a second
  consumer once export (F2) lands. Neither consumer's output has a test that
  fails when its shape changes.
- 2026-10-25 - Strategic finding, filed as A1: a `tests/test_contracts.py`
  that runs the real CLI (`python -m shelf ...` subprocess, so stdout is exactly
  what the sync job sees). It covers empty and non-empty `list --json`, and the
  export format once [export-format](decision-export-format.md) is decided.
  Persistence (F8) has to keep these tests passing across restarts.

import argparse
import json

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    ls = sub.add_parser("list")
    ls.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        rows = books.all_books()
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(rows) if rows else "")
        else:
            for b in rows:
                print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0
"""The catalogue, in memory."""
_BOOKS = []


def add(title, author):
    book = {"title": title, "author": author}
    _BOOKS.append(book)
    return book


def find(query):
    return [b for b in _BOOKS if query in b["title"]]


def all_books():
    return list(_BOOKS)


def clear():
    _BOOKS.clear()
# shelf

A book catalogue CLI, in memory.

    python -m shelf add "Dune" "Frank Herbert"
    python -m shelf find Dune
    python -m shelf list --json
    python -m shelf report

`list --json` is read every night by the library's sync job, which parses the
output with `json.loads`. Board: TICKETS.md. Tests: `python -m pytest`.

Choose CSV with a fixed `title,author` header and make that header the contract A1 tests.

**Risk others may not see:** CSV going to stdout on Windows is fragile. Writing `csv` to text-mode stdout gives `\r\r\n`, which shows up as blank rows in Excel. 1	# Decision: persistence (JSON file next to the package, or SQLite) (F8)
2	
3	Sources: [goal](goal.md); TICKETS.md F8, A2; `shelf/books.py` at `1c182c9`;
4	board seat agents 2026-10-25: architect `a2e38730f469ae84d`, ops
5	`a3efe380c61312539`, library staff (in UX's place) `ab1c5e8c050a49eb1`,
6	product `ad29598dbcc08eba5`. They ran one at a time ([pref](pref-owner.md)).
7	
8	## History
9	- 2026-10-25 - The owner put persistence in v1 and left the format open. Its
10	  stakeholders are the nightly sync job, the library's spreadsheet people and
11	  the next maintainer ([goal](goal.md)). As of `1c182c9` the catalogue is a module-level
12	  list in `shelf/books.py`, lost on exit.
13	- 2026-10-25 - Score 5 (base 1, +1 domains: storage, sync job, spreadsheet,
14	  maintenance; +1 hard to reverse: an on-disk format; +1 seats expected to
15	  disagree; +1 changes what consumers do). Board convened, seats run one at
16	  a time ([pref](pref-owner.md)). Status: open.
17	- 2026-10-25 - Board synthesis below. Status: open, waiting on the owner (Q1
18	  in the session report). Security was left off the board: there is no PII or
19	  access control in a title/author list. The library-staff seat replaced UX.
20	
21	## Board synthesis (2026-10-25)
22	
23	### Agree
24	- **Not next to the package** (all four seats). "Next to the package" is
25	  inside site-packages: a reinstall or upgrade wipes it, it may be read-only,
26	  and each virtualenv gets its own catalogue. Every seat proposed a per-user
27	  data directory (`%APPDATA%\shelf\`, `~/.local/share/shelf/`) with an
28	  environment-variable override, for tests and the sync host.
29	- **Atomic writes** (all four): write a temp file, then `os.replace`, so the
30	  nightly `list --json` never reads a half-written store.
31	- **The store is private** (architect, ops, product): the contracts are
32	  `list --json` stdout and the export. Nobody reads the storage file directly,
33	  so the format stays reversible behind `shelf/books.py`. The README should say so.
34	
35	### The disagreement
36	Ops wants **SQLite**: atomic transactions and consistent reads while `add`
37	runs, plus hot backup (`.backup`) and restore without stopping anything.
38	Architect, library staff and product want **JSON**: stdlib, diffable, and a
39	librarian or the next maintainer can open it in Notepad. They see SQLite's
40	advantages (concurrent writers, scale, queries) as F7-era needs. Ops would
41	accept JSON if the atomic-replace rule holds. Library staff would switch to
42	SQLite if several people write from a shared drive.
43	What it is really about: **whether v1 has concurrent writers**. If there are
44	none, JSON plus atomic replace is enough. If there are, JSON's lost-update
45	risk is real.
46	
47	### Actions
48	1. Implement the owner's choice behind the existing `books.py` API: path
49	   resolution (env var, then per-user dir), atomic save, load on start.
50	   README notes the store is private. Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: F8.
51	2. Make a missing or corrupt store a loud error, not an empty shelf. The
52	   sync job would otherwise ingest `[]` as healthy and might wipe its side.
53	   Corrupt JSON should name the bad line, and the previous copy should be kept
54	   as `.bak` (ops, library staff). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A2.
55	3. Find out which OS user and machine the nightly sync job runs as. A per-user
56	   data dir only works if `add` and the sync job share a user, or if the env var
57	   is set on the sync host. Owner: **the owner**. Ticket: F8 blocker.
58	4. Contract test that the catalogue survives a restart (subprocess `add`,
59	   then a new subprocess `list --json`). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A1.
60	
61	### The owner's decision
62	Will anything write the catalogue concurrently in v1, for example the sync job
63	writing back, or several staff on a shared drive?
64	- **A** - No: **JSON file** in the per-user data dir, with an env-var override
65	  and atomic replace. Readable by anyone, stdlib, cheapest to build and
66	  maintain. Costs: lost updates if concurrent writers appear later (migrating
67	  behind `books.py` is cheap while the store stays private).
68	- **B** - Yes, or not sure: **SQLite** at the same location. Safe concurrent
69	  access and hot backup. Costs: opaque to staff and to Notepad, plus a schema
70	  the next maintainer owns.
71	- **C** - As briefed: **JSON file next to the package**. All four seats were
72	  against it; a reinstall loses the catalogue.
73	
74	Recommendation (the chief's): **A**. Three seats chose it outright and ops
75	accepts it under the atomic-replace rule. While the store stays private the
76	choice is reversible, so v1 does not pay for concurrency it may not have.
77

import argparse
import json

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    ls = sub.add_parser("list")
    ls.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        rows = books.all_books()
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(rows) if rows else "")
        else:
            for b in rows:
                print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0
===README
# shelf

A book catalogue CLI, in memory.

    python -m shelf add "Dune" "Frank Herbert"
    python -m shelf find Dune
    python -m shelf list --json
    python -m shelf report

`list --json` is read every night by the library's sync job, which parses the
output with `json.loads`. Board: TICKETS.md. Tests: `python -m pytest`.

summary:
**Position:** CSV. The nightly sync job already has its machine contract, `list --json`, so the export should serve the person who opens it, which is the spreadsheet staff. A JSON export would just be `list --json` written to a file: a second machine contract that A1 has to test and that can drift. Backups should copy the store itself (atomic copy of the F8 file), not go through export.

**Strongest reason:** one machine contract per consumer. The sync job keeps `list --json`, the spreadsheet gets CSV, and A1 tests each one exactly once.

**Risk others may not see:** byte-level problems on Windows. Shell redirection can mangle the file: Windows PowerShell 5.1's `>` writes UTF-16, and `print` of csv rows gives `\r\r\n` line endings. Accented author names turn into garbled characters in Excel without a UTF-8 BOM. A title starting with `=` runs as a formula. So:
- `export` should write to `-o PATH` itself, as `utf-8-sig` with `newline=""`.
- It should always write a header row, so an empty shelf gives a header, not a blank file (the B6 lesson).
- A1 should check the actual bytes on disk, not just whether they parse.

**What would change my mind:** if export is meant to be the restore or sync-interchange format (a planned `import`, or the sync job switching to export), I'd want JSON there. The cheap compromise would be `--format csv|json` with CSV as the default.

# Decision: export format, CSV or JSON (F2, F5)

Sources: TICKETS.md F2, F5, A1 at `1c182c9`; board seat agents 2026-10-25:
library staff `ab5a7adb8d4cf9662`, architect `ae40976c74f5f8fc5`, ops
`a06a437e2de5607c0` (one at a time, [pref](pref-owner.md)).

## History
- 2026-10-25 - F2 marks the format as the owner's call, not decided yet. CSV
  opens in the library's spreadsheet. JSON matches `list --json`. F5 builds
  on F2, so both wait for this decision.
- 2026-10-25 - Score 5 (base 1, +1 domains: spreadsheet and sync-job
  consumers; +1 hard to reverse once people build on the file; +1 seats
  expected to disagree; +1 changes what the spreadsheet people do). Board
  convened after [persistence](decision-persistence.md), which it overlaps.
  Status: open.
- 2026-10-25 - Board synthesis below. The three seats agreed. Status: open,
  waiting on the owner (Q2 in the session report). F2 says this is the owner's call.

## Board synthesis (2026-10-25)

### Agree
- **CSV** (all three seats). The sync job already has its machine contract,
  `list --json`. A JSON export would add a second contract that has to stay in
  step with the first, and it would give nothing to the only other consumer,
  the spreadsheet people, who double-click files.
- **Write a file, not stdout** (all three). `python -m shelf export > x.csv`
  breaks on Windows: PowerShell 5.1's `>` writes UTF-16, and csv rows through
  `print` come out as `\r\r\n` (blank rows in Excel). So `export` writes
  `-o PATH` itself, as `utf-8-sig` (a BOM, so "García Márquez" survives in
  Excel), with `newline=""`.
- **The bytes are the contract** (all three). Every export has a `title,author`
  header row, so an empty shelf gives the header alone (the B6 lesson). Quoting
  is `QUOTE_MINIMAL`. Cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading
  `'`, against formula injection (library staff, architect). A1 tests the bytes
  on disk.

### The disagreement
None surfaced on the format. All three made it conditional on one fact: who
reads the export. If a program will parse it, or it is the backup and restore
format (a future `import`), every seat would want JSON, or `--format csv|json`
(ops).
What it is really about: **is export for people or for programs?**

### Actions
1. Once the owner confirms: build F2 to the byte rules above (`dump()`
   returns the text; `export -o PATH` writes it). Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: F2.
2. F5 (`author=` filter) on top of it. Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: F5.
3. Add the export bytes to the contract tests. Owner: implementer agent. Ticket: A1.
4. Ask the spreadsheet people whether their Excel uses a semicolon locale. If
   it does, the delimiter becomes `;` or a flag. Owner: **the owner**.

### The owner's decision
Is the export for people (the spreadsheet staff) or also for programs or restore?
- **A** - People only: **CSV**, with the byte rules above. Opens on
  double-click. Costs: not a lossless restore format; backups copy the store
  instead (ops).
- **B** - Both: **CSV by default, `--format json`** as well. Covers a future
  import. Costs: a second JSON contract to test and keep in step with `list --json`.
- **C** - Programs: **JSON**. Matches `list --json`. Costs: the spreadsheet
  people can't open it.

Recommendation (the chief's): **A**. All three seats chose it, and B can be
added later without breaking anyone.

Load `skillator:relay-morpheus` (run file, chain, worktrees), `skillator:tickets-zordon` (the board) and `skillator:tasks-sentinels` (one fresh implementer per task) and work the tickets to the end with subagents. Arguments: `B3 B4 B6 F3 A1 1`

**Arguments.** An optional agent count first, then optional ticket IDs (`2 F12 F14`, `max`, `F12`).
The count is a whole number of at least 1 or `max`; no count = 1. No IDs = every open ticket on
TICKETS.md (`[ ]`, `[~]`, `[!]` re-checked). A first word that is neither a count nor a ticket ID
(`0`, `two`) → say it is not a count and stop.
- 1 (the default): serial, one agent at a time - the one-agent-at-a-time rule.
- N > 1: up to N stages at once, each in its own stage worktree off the run branch, merged back
  on landing. `max`: as many as are file-disjoint, no fixed cap.
- Tickets whose files overlap never run together, whatever the count.

1. **Pick.** First `ticket-meta pick [IDs]` (tickets-zordon, F80): only its `pick` lines run - unassigned
   tickets and yours; each `skip <ID> <owner>` is listed as skipped with its owner, never run.
   Then skip `[%]` (owner checks), `[>]` deferred, `[x]` and `[-]`; say which were skipped
   and why. Nothing left → say so and stop.
2. **Plan** (relay-morpheus, its chain reference): `init` one run over TICKETS.md - one stage per
   ticket, then the main session's final verify-review-bump-commit-push stage. `chain plan` each
   ticket stage with `--files` (what the ticket names or will touch) and its exact prompt file
   before the first dispatch; a ticket sharing files with an earlier one gets `--after` it. `chain
   plan` and `chain dispatch` claim each ticket for you (`ticket-meta claim`); a refused claim is
   said in the report. Every
   prompt says: work and commit in the run worktree (or the stage worktree dispatch names), never
   the main checkout, never push, never edit TICKETS.md.
   With grayskull-power on (`.skillator/grayskull.md` present) every prompt opens with this line, and without it does not: `Load skillator:code-yoda first (restraint, full): the smallest diff that meets the ticket - no speculative abstraction, no new dependency, no refactor outside the ticket, no ceremony; run its review lens on your diff before /code-review and cut what it flags.`
3. **Dispatch** - one fresh implementer per ticket (tasks-sentinels): the Agent tool, given only that
   stage's stored prompt, no session history. `chain decide`, then `chain dispatch <n>` before
   each agent: it writes the row and the exact prompt into the run file first. Count 1: `chain
   next`, one stage at a time. N or `max`: `RELAY_CHAIN_PARALLEL=<N>` (`max` = the number of
   ticket stages) on `chain next --all`, one dispatch and one agent per `NEXT` line; refill the
   free slots after each landing.
4. **Land** each stage when its own agent returns: read the diff, regression sweep, `/code-review` (`code-review:code-review`) on the staged diff;
   fix findings through a new implementer. A stage in its own worktree: `chain merge <n>` first
   (exit 3 = conflict: the stage is `!`, a retry stage is planned on the merged branch). Then
   `stage <n> x <sha>` and flip its ticket with tickets-zordon's ticket-meta (`board <ID> <mark>`
   from a worktree). A failed stage: `!`, its In-flight block kept with the failure.
5. **Finish**: merge the run branch into main from the main checkout, remove the run worktree and
   branch, bump the version where the repo's rule says so, then ask before the push - never push
   unasked. Headless or no answer: stop there and say `push: waiting for the owner`.

Park the owner's questions for one end batch; the six stops are asked the moment they are reached.

# relay-morpheus — staged runs that outlive the session

A staged run has two records. The transcript, which dies with the session, and
the tree, which does not. Everything that matters has to be in the second one
**while the run is still going**, because there is no guarantee you reach the
end to write it down.

## The rule

```
WRITE THE STAGE DOWN BEFORE YOU DISPATCH IT, NOT AFTER IT COMES BACK
```

This is the one thing this skill exists for, and it is the one thing three
isolated baseline runs did not do (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-morpheus.txt`).
All three executed a four-stage plan end to end and left no on-disk record of
progress until the very last write — one left none at all. A session ending
anywhere before that leaves a working tree full of unattributed diff and no way
to tell which stages produced it, which were finished, or what was still
running.

Reading a mid-run tree is **not** this skill's problem. The companion baseline
(`scenario-relay-morpheus-resume.txt`) shows a fresh session doing that correctly
unprompted, against pressure to trust stale checkboxes. Relay adds nothing
there and says nothing about it.

**Violating the letter of this is violating the spirit of it.** "I'll record it
when the stage returns" is the failure, not a variation on it — the stages that
need recording most are the ones that never return.

## Handing a run to another session

Every run gets a short number when it is created, and `init` prints the
sentence that resumes it:

```
hand this to any session:  continue RUN-0003
```

That sentence is the whole interface. A fresh session — another machine,
another host, a colleague — needs nothing else: **"continue RUN-0003"**. It has no
transcript, so the ledger is what it reads, and the ledger is on disk because
it was written before the work, not after.

```sh
relay-morpheus.sh list          # every run, what is open, and its resume sentence
relay-morpheus.sh resume 3      # everything a session that has never seen it needs
relay-morpheus.sh 3 status      # any command takes the id first
```

**One name, everywhere (F44).** A run is `RUN-0003`: its serial number,
zero-padded to four digits (more past 9999, never cut). That one name is the run
file (`run-0003-<slug>.md`), its `# RUN-0003` header, its branch and worktree,
its queue row and the resume sentence. `RUN-0003`, `RUN-3`, `run-3` and `3` all
resolve to the same run, because whoever types it next is working from memory
of a conversation rather than from a path - and a run named before F44
(`run-3-*.md`, `# RUN-3`) is found by every spelling too, and listed padded.
With one run open and no id given, that run is assumed; with two or more, the
script refuses rather than guessing.

**Run owners (F44).** A run can be given to a team member: `relay-morpheus.sh
[<id>] owner @asha` (`-Mode owner [-Id n] -Text @asha`) writes an `owner: @asha`
line in the run file's header, `owner -` clears it, and `init --owner @asha`
(`-RunOwner @asha`) sets it at the start. Handles come from tickets-zordon's
`.skillator/team.md` (`- @asha: asha@x.com`); a handle not in it is refused, and
with no team file any well-formed `@handle` is taken, with a note. `list`,
`resume`, `status` and `queue-run list` show the owner.

## The run file

`.skillator/run-<0000>-<slug>.md`, one per run, in the repo. Markdown because a human and any
host both have to read it with no tooling. Git-tracked by default; a repo that
objects can `.gitignore` it and lose only the shared view, not the resume.

```markdown
# RUN-0007 — notekeep v2
plan: docs/plans/PLAN-notekeep.md
started: 2026-09-22T09:14Z   updated: 2026-09-22T10:02Z
owner: @asha

## Stages
| # | stage | state | owner | heartbeat | landed |
|---|-------|-------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 41 | list --json     | x | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T09:22Z | 3f1a2c9 |
| 42 | tags + --tag    | ~ | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T10:02Z | - |
| 43 | export          |   | -            | -     | - |
| 44 | README          |   | -            | -     | - |

## In flight
### stage 42 — tags + --tag  (dispatched 09:51)
prompt: |
  Add a `tags` list to each note in notekeep/store.py and a `list --tag <t>`
  filter in notekeep/cli.py. Test both. Do not touch export or the README.
last seen: wrote store.py, tests not yet run.

## Rulings
- 09:38 — stage 41 emits `[]` not `null` for an empty store — the plan does not
  say, JSON consumers expect a list — costs a one-line change if wrong.
```

**States:** `` (pending) · `~` in flight · `x` landed · `!` failed · `?`
parked (chain only: every item waits on a decision) · `>` re-planned (`landed`
names the new stage).
**`landed`** is a commit sha or a path, never a claim. An empty `landed` on an
`x` row is a lie the next session will believe.
**One run, one worktree (F35).** In a git repo with a commit, `init` also
creates the run's own worktree, `<repo>/.skillator/worktrees/RUN-0007-<slug>`
(git-ignored, inside the repo so dispatched agents may work there), on
branch `run/RUN-0007-<slug>`, and writes both into the run file's header. Every
stage of the run works and commits **there** - say so in each dispatch prompt -
never in the main checkout, whose index another run may be using. The run
file itself stays in the main checkout's `.skillator/`, whichever worktree
calls the script. `resume` names the worktree and recreates it from its branch
if it is gone. `init --here` (`-Here`) keeps the old one-checkout behaviour.
The run reaches main through its final stage: merge `run/RUN-<n>-<slug>` from
the main checkout, then `git worktree remove <worktree>` and
`git branch -d run/RUN-<n>-<slug>` - nothing removes them for you.
**Leases across runs (F36).** `chain dispatch` leases the stage's `files:` in
one registry per clone (`<git-common-dir>/skillator/leases`); a file another
run's live stage holds refuses the dispatch (`LEASED <path> RUN-m stage s`,
exit 2) and `chain next` shows the stage `IDLE ... leased`. Landing, failing
or re-planning releases; a lease silent past 20 min is taken, with a ruling.
Board edits from a run worktree go through `relay-morpheus.sh board <ID>
<mark>` (`-Mode board -Ticket -Mark`), which writes the main checkout's
`TICKETS.md` under its lock.
**Only my tickets (F80).** A run takes only tickets that are unassigned or the
session person's own (tickets-zordon `ticket-meta pick`; no `team.md` = every
ticket, as before). A stage whose `tickets:` name one someone else owns is
`IDLE <n> owned <ID> <owner>` in `chain next` - listed as skipped with its
owner, never run - and its `chain dispatch` is refused (exit 2). `chain plan`
and `chain dispatch` claim the stage's tickets (`ticket-meta claim`: `[owner:
<me>]`, box kept); at plan a refused claim is a `note:` on stderr, at dispatch
the claim is the gate - before the row flips, refused (exit 2) when someone
else owns or claimed a ticket first. Ownership ticket-meta cannot tell (its
`pick` fails while a `team.md` exists) counts as owned: `owned <ID> ?`. `FINAL`
names the stages skipped as someone else's.
**Parallel stages (F37).** `chain next --all` names every stage that can run
now - files disjoint from what is in flight and from each other - capped at 2
below 50 % of the 5-hour window, else 1. A stage that runs beside another works
in its own worktree off the run branch; `chain merge <n>` brings it back (exit
3 on a conflict: the stage fails). [references/chain.md](references/chain.md).
**A marathon of runs (F38).** Runs wait in one queue (`queue-run add|next|
start|pause|done`), run one at a time, and land on main one at a time
(`land <n> --start`, review and bump on the run branch, `land <n> --finish`);
one end batch across runs (`queue --all`), one push per marathon, and an away
flow (`away on|off`) that notifies, waits 30 minutes and moves on - never a
default. [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md).
**Numbers are serial across the project, not per run.** `init` takes the RUN
id and every stage number from the F21 allocator (`practice/scripts/next-id.sh`,
kinds `RUN` and `S`), which reads every run file in the tree and on every ref
and keeps a counter every worktree of the clone shares — so two worktrees never
both make RUN-4, and a new run's first stage continues after the highest stage
any run has used (RUN-0007 above starts at 41). "Stage 42" names one stage in the
whole project. Existing run files are never renumbered.
**Rulings** are appended, never rewritten — see `tasks-sentinels`, which is
where they come from and which writes into this same file.

## The loop

1. **Before dispatch** — add or update the stage row to `~`, write the In-flight
   block with the *exact prompt you are about to send*, stamp the heartbeat.
   Prompt not written down → the agent is not recoverable → do not dispatch.
2. **While it runs** — re-stamp the heartbeat whenever the agent reports. A
   stale heartbeat is the only signal you get that a network drop took it;
   `hooks/relay-morpheus.* orphans` turns that into a list.
3. **When it lands** — commit the stage's work, then set `x` and put the sha in
   `landed`; `stage <n> x` (and `>`) drops its In-flight block. In that order:
   the sha cannot be written before the commit exists.
4. **When it fails** — `!`, and leave the In-flight block where it is with the
   failure appended. A failed stage's prompt is the thing you need most.
5. **Never** delete a row. A run file only grows.

Stages that touch the same files do not run at once; independent ones do
(`PRACTICE.md` §4). Either way each gets its row before it gets its agent.

## Resuming

Open `.skillator/run.md`, then check it against the tree — the file is written
before the work, so the last `~` row is a stage that *started*, not one that
finished. `landed` shas are ground truth; anything else is a claim to verify.
Redispatch straight from the stored prompt; the rows are keyed by stage number,
so a redispatch that duplicates work overwrites rather than appends.

Then carry on. A resume does not need permission to continue — see
`grayskull-power` §3, **run to the end**.

## Chaining ticket workflows

When the stages are ticket workflows that start each other — "work every open
ticket in staged workflows, keep going" — the rule above gains a second half:

```
THE NEXT STAGE IS STARTED BY THE LAST ONE'S COMPLETION, AND BY NOTHING
ELSE UNTIL USAGE SAYS SO
```

Two isolated runs (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-chain*.txt`) dispatched
with no plan on disk, read no usage between stages, named stages by their
content (two runs picked the same name), and started a stage at 84 % of the
5-hour window. So a chain is run **only** by the loop in
[references/chain.md](references/chain.md): every stage `chain plan`ned with
its code and exact prompt before the first dispatch; `chain decide` (on
`usage-watch level`) before every stage, the first included; `chain hold` at 80 % and a `chain wait` listener instead
of a new stage; `mode:` in the run file naming what was actually dispatched.
Read that file before the first `chain` command.

Every chain is a **marathon**: a question only the user can answer is parked
on disk (`park`), the chain goes on with every stage that does not wait on it
(`chain next`), and the queue is asked once, at the end. The six stops are
never parked:

```
A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION -
NEVER AS ONE ITEM OF THE END BATCH
```

Two baseline runs (`scenario-marathon-stop.txt`) left an untracked directory
alone, said its deletion could not be undone, and then asked it as item 2 of 3
beside a format question. Read [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md)
when a verdict carries `parked`, a stop fires, or `chain next` prints `ASK` or
`UNBLOCK`. `/marathon-plan` and `/marathon-run` (F73) are its last section: a
marathon saved as a Workflow script (`templates/marathon-workflow.js`), then run.

## Scripts

`hooks/relay-morpheus.sh` · `hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1` — the same commands, mirrored per
`PLATFORMS.md`: `init`, `add`, `stage`, `heartbeat`, `status`, `orphans`, and
`chain plan|dispatch|hold|release|wait|status|decide|next|edge`, and the
marathon's `park`, `answer`, `queue`. They are
bookkeeping, not judgement; every one reads or edits `.skillator/run.md` and
nothing else. Run `selftest` on both after touching either.
`watchdog hold "<why>" | release | status` (F48, the ops-board mod on red disk/memory) holds every new `chain dispatch` and GREEN harness `run`, exit 2, until released.
`chain decide --level "<level line>"` (F49) decides on a reading the caller already has.

```sh
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  init plan.md "notekeep v2" "list --json" "tags" "export" "README"
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  add "docs pass"                    # a stage found mid-run; prints 45
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 '~' build:sonnet          # before you dispatch
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 x  build:sonnet 3f1a2c9   # after you commit
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  orphans 20                         # who has gone quiet
```

```powershell
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode init  -Plan plan.md -Title "notekeep v2" -Stages "list --json,tags,export,README"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode add   -Title "docs pass"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State '~' -Owner build:sonnet
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State x   -Owner build:sonnet -Landed 3f1a2c9
# In a headless or nested run on Windows, call the .sh through the Bash tool:
# the PowerShell tool refuses `& <script>.ps1` and `powershell -File` under any
# allow rule (A91, claude 2.1.280).
```

Add rows with `add`, never by hand: a hand-typed number is the per-run
restart this numbering removed. The scripts find the allocator beside the
installed skills (`<skills>/practice/scripts/`, or `<root>/practice/scripts/`
in a clone or the plugin cache; `RELAY_NEXT_ID` overrides). Without it they
fall back to the old local rule and say so on stderr — numbers then repeat
across worktrees.

Three constraints the pair has to keep, each learned the hard way:

- **Pure ASCII, and the empty cell is `-`, not an em dash.** Windows PowerShell
  5.1 reads a BOM-less script as ANSI and corrupts anything above 126.
- **The run file is LF with no BOM, written to a temp and moved.** Both mirrors
  edit the same file, so one of them flipping encoding rewrites every line in
  the diff; and a kill between truncate and write would empty the only record
  of what was in flight.
- **`-Stages` takes `"a,b,c"` and pending is spelled `pending`.** PowerShell's
  `-File` passes each argument as one literal string and drops empty ones, and
  `-File` is how every hook here invokes it.

### Seeing a run without being told about one

`list` prints every run with its resume sentence, and prints nothing when there
are none, so it is safe as a `SessionStart` hook. With one wired, a session that inherits
a half-finished run sees it in its own context before the user has to remember
to mention it — which is the difference between resuming and starting over.

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [ {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"<SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1\" -Mode list",
  "timeout": 5
} ] } ] } }
```

macOS/Linux: `sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh list`. Forward slashes throughout —
PowerShell accepts them and it removes all backslash-escaping from the JSON.
Other hosts have no equivalent event; there, reading `.skillator/run.md` is the
first thing `resume-cortana` does. `watch-cortana` already drains in-flight
agents at the limit — relay is what it drains *into*, so the two do not overlap.
